Should this keep the previous release-tag fallback?

This changes the checkout from `inputs.cdk_ref || inputs.release_tag` to `inputs.cdk_ref || github.ref`. For manual dispatch, or any helper that omits `cdk_ref`, that can publish `release_tag` while building from the workflow branch instead of the release tag.

Could we keep this as:

```yaml
ref: ${{ inputs.cdk_ref || inputs.release_tag }}
```

Same issue applies to the other CDK checkout steps in this workflow.

+              platforms: [.iOS(.v14), .macOS(.v13)],
+              products: [
+                  .library(name: "Cdk", targets: ["Cdk"]),
+              ],
+              targets: [
+                  .binaryTarget(
+                      name: "CashuDevKitFFI",
+                      url: "https://github.com/${{ vars.CDK_SWIFT_REPO }}/releases/download/${TAG}/CashuDevKitFFI.xcframework.zip",
+                      checksum: "${XCFRAMEWORK_CHECKSUM}"
+                  ),
+                  .target(
+                      name: "Cdk",
+                      dependencies: ["CashuDevKitFFI"],
+                      path: "Sources/Cdk"
+                  ),
+              ]
+          )
+          EOF
+
+      - name: Commit to release branch
+        working-directory: cdk-swift
+        run: |
+          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+          git add -A
+          git diff --cached --quiet && echo "No changes to commit" && exit 0
+          git commit -m "release: ${{ inputs.release_tag }} — add Swift sources and Package.swift"
+
+      - name: Merge to default branch
+        working-directory: cdk-swift

+          TAG="${{ inputs.release_tag }}"
+          RELEASE_BRANCH="release/v${TAG#v}"

+          echo "DEFAULT_BRANCH=${DEFAULT_BRANCH}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+          echo "RELEASE_BRANCH=${RELEASE_BRANCH}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+          git checkout "${DEFAULT_BRANCH}"
+          git merge "${RELEASE_BRANCH}" --squash

+
+      - name: Push release branch
+        working-directory: cdk-swift
+        run: |
+          git checkout "${RELEASE_BRANCH}"
+          git push origin "${RELEASE_BRANCH}"
+
+      - name: Create release on cdk-swift (creates tag and uploads asset)
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SWIFT_DEPLOY_KEY }}
+        run: |
+          gh release create "${{ inputs.release_tag }}" \
+            --repo ${{ vars.CDK_SWIFT_REPO }} \

comment.body:
Should this target a ref that already contains the generated `Package.swift` and Swift sources?

At this point the local default branch has the squash commit from `git merge "${RELEASE_BRANCH}" --squash`, but it has not been pushed yet. `gh release create --target "${DEFAULT_BRANCH}"` resolves against the remote branch, so the release tag can be created from the old default-branch tip. SwiftPM would then resolve `vX.Y.Z` to package contents that do not include the generated sources/checksum for this release.

Could we either push the default branch before creating the release, or create the release tag against a pushed release ref/commit that already contains these files? The Kotlin flow avoids partially pushed refs by publishing first and pushing tags/branches during cleanup; for Swift we need both retry-safe ordering and a tag target that contains the package contents.

issue.title: Move XCFramework build to CI and streamline local dev workflow
issue.body:
I'm reopening #1972 since my local repo was messed up and Github closed that ticket

Replace the monolithic generate-bindings.sh script with a CI-driven swift-publish workflow that builds the XCFramework and syncs sources to the cdk-swift distribution repo. This separates the heavy cross-compilation (iOS device, iOS simulator, macOS universal) from the local development loop.

Local changes:
- Rework `ffi-generate-swift` justfile recipe to set up an SPM-compatible package structure (Sources/Cdk, Sources/cdk_ffiFFI) using the dylib from `ffi-build`, enabling `swift test` without building XCFrameworks
- Add `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` to CI and `test-swift` so the dynamic library is found at runtime
- Gate bip353 FFI exports behind `feature = "bip353"` to allow the Swift FFI crate to opt out of features that pull in heavy DNS dependencies
- Pin cdk-ffi dependency in Swift crate to only `npubcash` and `bip353` features (no default features) for a leaner build
- Add Swift SPM generated artifacts to .gitignore
- Remove the now-unused `binding-swift` justfile target
- Add bindings/swift/README.md with SPM and Xcode installation docs
- Update bindings/README.md to reflect the new CI-driven build flow

issue.title: feat: add p2pk_signing_keys to SendOptions
issue.body:
Add `p2pk_signing_keys: Vec<SecretKey>` and `allow_locked_proofs: bool` to `SendOptions` so wallets holding P2PK-locked proofs can spend them through the standard `prepare_send` / `confirm` flow without a separate manual swap.

Behaviour
---------
- When `p2pk_signing_keys` is non-empty and `allow_locked_proofs` is false (the default), all selected proofs are routed through a swap so the resulting token contains fresh, unconditioned proofs.
- Setting `allow_locked_proofs: true` opts in to the less-private passthrough path: proofs are signed and retain their spending conditions in the token. This is useful for multi-hop or offline flows where the next holder intentionally receives signed-but-still-locked proofs.

SIG_ALL incompatibility
-----------------------
`SigFlag::SigAll` is incompatible with passthrough signing: the signature would need to commit to swap outputs that do not exist at signing time. `confirm()` now calls `enforce_sig_flag()` on the proofs-to-send set and returns `nut11::Error::SigAllNotSupportedHere` early rather than silently producing an unspendable token.

Changes
-------
- `cdk-common`: add `p2pk_signing_keys` and `allow_locked_proofs` to `SendOptions`, with doc comments explaining the SigAll incompatibility.
- `cdk/wallet/util.rs`: extract `sign_proofs()` with four unit tests covering correct key, wrong key, plain proof, and empty-keys cases.
- `cdk/wallet/send/saga/mod.rs`: shadow `force_swap` to `true` in `internal_prepare` when signing keys are provided and passthrough is not opted in; call `sign_proofs()` in `confirm()` for both `proofs_to_swap` (default path) and `proofs_to_send` (passthrough path); add SigAll check with an explanatory block comment before the passthrough signing block.
- `cdk-ffi`: add `p2pk_signing_keys` and `allow_locked_proofs` to FFI `SendOptions` and update both `From` conversions.
- Integration tests: add four pure tests covering the normal signing flow, the exact-denomination short-circuit regression, the passthrough opt-in, and the SigAll rejection.

### Description

Add `p2pk_signing_keys: Vec<SecretKey>` and `allow_locked_proofs: bool` to `SendOptions` so wallets holding P2PK-locked proofs can spend them through the standard `prepare_send` / `confirm` flow without a separate manual swap.

**Default behaviour** (`allow_locked_proofs: false`): all selected proofs are routed through a swap, producing a clean token with no spending conditions. The caller provides signing keys only to authorize the swap inputs.

**Passthrough** (`allow_locked_proofs: true`): proofs are signed in-place and retain their spending conditions. Useful for multi-hop or offline flows where the next holder intentionally receives signed-but-still-locked proofs.

**SigAll rejection**: `SigFlag::SigAll` is incompatible with passthrough because the signature would need to commit to swap outputs that don't exist at signing time. `confirm()` detects this via `enforce_sig_flag()` and returns `nut11::Error::SigAllNotSupportedHere` early rather than silently producing an unspendable token.

Also fixes a force-swap short-circuit bug where proofs summing exactly to the send amount bypassed the swap entirely, causing locked proofs to escape into the token unsigned.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p cdk wallet::util` — 5 unit tests pass
- [ ] `test_p2pk_send_options_signing_keys` — normal signing flow
- [ ] `test_p2pk_signing_keys_exact_denomination_short_circuit` — force-swap regression
- [ ] `test_p2pk_allow_locked_proofs_passthrough` — passthrough opt-in
- [ ] `test_p2pk_allow_locked_proofs_rejects_sig_all` — SigAll rejection

I would like to create ecash where there is a new unit that the mint rotates to every epoch. The unit string would be something like `credit-<T>` and then tomorrow it would be `credit-<T + 1>`. 

mintd already supports a custom unit string allowing for any arbitrary unit via ` CurrencyUnit::Custom(String)`, but the payment processors are registered at startup and then immutable at runtime. Also, `rotate_keyset` already seems to allow for creating and activating a new unit keyset.

I should be able to call the grpc interface to register a new unit at the start of every epoch without restarting the mint. Previous units will have their own expiry and should not be deactivated when the new unit is registered. A payment processor should be able to support registration of these variable unit strings at runtime.

issue.title: feat(payment-processor): propagate mint quote_id to backend
issue.body:
### Description

<!-- Describe the purpose of this PR, what's being adding and/or fixed -->

Adds the mint's QuoteId to the three OutgoingPaymentOptions struct variants so custom payment-method backends can deterministically correlate their `get_payment_quote` and `make_payment` calls for the same melt.

Today, the gRPC payment-processor proto carries no link between those two calls for the same melt: a backend's `get_payment_quote` returns a PaymentQuoteResponse whose `request_lookup_id` the mint stores on the quote, but the eventual `make_payment` receives an OutgoingPaymentOptions with neither the stored lookup_id nor the mint's quote_id (`from_melt_quote_with_fee` in cdk-common drops `extra_json` and has no quote_id field). bolt11/bolt12 backends are insulated by the payment_hash / offer being intrinsically derivable from the invoice in both calls. Custom backends have no such anchor, and have to fabricate a derivation — typically hashing `request` — which forces the wallet to make `request` unique per melt. That's awkward for any custom rail whose "request" doesn't naturally carry uniqueness (branch tickets, account IDs, free-text references). With `quote_id` plumbed through, the backend has the same stable key the mint uses everywhere else, so correlation is trivial.

Changes:
- cdk-common::payment: add `quote_id: QuoteId` to Bolt11/Bolt12/Custom OutgoingPaymentOptions structs. Propagate it in `from_melt_quote_with_fee` from `melt_quote.id`.
- cdk::mint::melt: pre-generate the quote_id before each `get_payment_quote` call (bolt11, bolt12, custom paths) and pass it both to the backend and to `MeltQuote::new`, replacing the previous implicit auto-generation.
- payment_processor.proto: add `optional string quote_id` to Bolt11/Bolt12/CustomOutgoingPaymentOptions and PaymentQuoteRequest. Field-numbers appended (5/6/7/6) to preserve wire compatibility with the existing fields. `optional` is used so the server can distinguish "not sent" from "sent empty" and emit a clear error for old clients.
- cdk-payment-processor server/client: serialize/deserialize quote_id. The server treats absence as a protocol error (defense-in-depth backing the version check, since the optional proto field would otherwise default silently).
- cdk-common: bump PAYMENT_PROCESSOR_PROTOCOL_VERSION 2.0.0 -> 3.0.0. The VersionInterceptor's strict equality check means any old mint/backend pair will see a clear "Protocol version mismatch" at connection time instead of misbehaving silently.
- cdk-integration-tests: extend the existing custom-payment-processor fixture to capture the received quote_id, and add a regression test asserting it matches the quote_id surfaced to the wallet.

The Rust API is intentionally non-optional (`quote_id: QuoteId`, not `Option<QuoteId>`): every legitimate caller site has the id available. The optional-ness lives at the proto/wire layer for explicit version detection.

issue.title: feat(cdk-axum): support redis-cluster for caching
issue.body:
closes #1578

### Description
This PR adds support for Redis Cluster and Valkey Cluster to the cdk-axum HTTP caching backend.

Currently, the cache only supports a single-node Redis connection, which fails in clustered environments because it cannot handle "MOVED" redirections. This change introduces a cluster-aware client that automatically routes requests to the correct nodes and handles cluster topology changes.

### Key Changes
1. Introduced `RedisClient` enum to support both Standard and Cluster connection types.

```yaml
with:
  ref: ${{ inputs.cdk_ref || inputs.release_tag }}
```

Should this mirror the Kotlin publish ordering? In `kotlin-publish.yml`, the workflow publishes to Maven Central before pushing the default branch and tag, which keeps retries cleaner if the actual package publish fails.

Here the default branch is pushed before `gh release create` uploads the XCFramework. If release creation or upload fails, retrying the workflow leaves the target repo partially published and may require manual cleanup. Could we delay pushing the default branch until after the release asset is created, or make the release step idempotent for an existing commit/tag?

issue.body:
## Support for Multi-Language Bindings in CI

### Motivation
We've decided to offer first-class support for **Kotlin**, **Swift**, and **Dart** bindings, with **Go** and **React Native** as secondary priorities. Previously, we had publishing workflows for [Kotlin](https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk-kotlin) and [Swift](https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk-swift), but these weren't tested in CDK's main CI. This led to breaking the bindings without noticing until release.

### Solution Overview
PR [#1706](https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/pull/1706) introduced binding builds and language-specific tests directly in CDK's main CI (currently Dart and Swift). This provides early feedback on breaking changes while minimizing non-Rust code in the main repository.

**Key principle:** The goal is to **build and test** bindings in the main CI, not to publish them. Publishing should remain in language-specific repositories to keep CDK's main repo focused on Rust.

### What's Needed
To complete this, we need to ensure that:
- Each language's build in CDK's main repo aligns as closely as possible with its release build in the language-specific repo
- All primary languages (Kotlin, Swift, Dart) have CI checks in place
- Secondary languages (Go, React Native) are considered for future implementation

### Next Steps
Sub-issues will be opened for each specific language to track their implementation.

Behaviour
---------
- When `p2pk_signing_keys` is non-empty and `allow_locked_proofs` is false (the default), all selected proofs are routed through a swap so the resulting token contains fresh, unconditioned proofs.
- Setting `allow_locked_proofs: true` opts in to the less-private passthrough path: proofs are signed and retain their spending conditions in the token. This is useful for multi-hop or offline flows where the next holder intentionally receives signed-but-still-locked proofs.

-----------------------
`SigFlag::SigAll` is incompatible with passthrough signing: the signature would need to commit to swap outputs that do not exist at signing time. `confirm()` now calls `enforce_sig_flag()` on the proofs-to-send set and returns `nut11::Error::SigAllNotSupportedHere` early rather than silently producing an unspendable token.

-------
- `cdk-common`: add `p2pk_signing_keys` and `allow_locked_proofs` to `SendOptions`, with doc comments explaining the SigAll incompatibility.
- `cdk/wallet/util.rs`: extract `sign_proofs()` with four unit tests covering correct key, wrong key, plain proof, and empty-keys cases.

Add `p2pk_signing_keys: Vec<SecretKey>` and `allow_locked_proofs: bool` to `SendOptions` so wallets holding P2PK-locked proofs can spend them through the standard `prepare_send` / `confirm` flow without a separate manual swap.

issue.body:
I'm reopening #1972 since my local repo was messed up and Github closed that ticket

Replace the monolithic generate-bindings.sh script with a CI-driven swift-publish workflow that builds the XCFramework and syncs sources to the cdk-swift distribution repo. This separates the heavy cross-compilation (iOS device, iOS simulator, macOS universal) from the local development loop.

Local changes:
- Rework `ffi-generate-swift` justfile recipe to set up an SPM-compatible package structure (Sources/Cdk, Sources/cdk_ffiFFI) using the dylib from `ffi-build`, enabling `swift test` without building XCFrameworks
- Add `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` to CI and `test-swift` so the dynamic library is found at runtime
- Gate bip353 FFI exports behind `feature = "bip353"` to allow the Swift FFI crate to opt out of features that pull in heavy DNS dependencies
- Pin cdk-ffi dependency in Swift crate to only `npubcash` and `bip353` features (no default features) for a leaner build
- Add Swift SPM generated artifacts to .gitignore
- Remove the now-unused `binding-swift` justfile target
- Add bindings/swift/README.md with SPM and Xcode installation docs
- Update bindings/README.md to reflect the new CI-driven build flow
